description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotional categories in a dataset used for evaluating speaker anonymization on emotional speech, with six distinct emotion labels represented as colored segments. The largest segment, labeled “Frustration” in light blue, accounts for 25.1% of the total. The second largest, “Neutral” in dark blue, comprises 23.1%. “Happiness,” shown in red, makes up 8.1%, while “Excitement,” in orange, represents 14.1%. “Sadness,” in yellow-orange, accounts for 14.7%, and “Anger,” in yellow, constitutes 14.9%. Each slice is clearly labeled with its emotion name and percentage value, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise order starting from the top: Frustration, Neutral, Happiness, Excitement, Sadness, and Anger. The chart does not include a separate legend, as labels and percentages are directly embedded within or adjacent to each slice. The visual proportions align closely with the numerical values, offering a clear comparative view of emotional distribution in the evaluated speech corpus.
